data.name: Rameshkant
data.gender_notes: Rameshkant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rameshkant is a popular Hindu name derived from the names of two major Hindu gods, Rama and Shank (Lord Shiva). Rama is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu and is known for his righteousness and courage. Lord Shiva, on the other hand, is the supreme god of the Hindu pantheon and the god of destruction and transformation. Combining the names of these two powerful deities in Rameshkant signifies a deep connection with the divine and a strong spiritual foundation.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name rooted in Hindu spirituality, symbolizing devotion and faith in the Hindu gods.
data.etymology: Rameshkant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's name Rama, Shank (Lord Shiva).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rameshkant total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Rameshkant was a Maratha warrior and the last king of the princely state of Jalkot in the Satara region, who led a fierce resistance against the British East India Company during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

Rameshkant was a renowned Hindu saint and a disciple of the 16th-century saint-philosopher Jñāneśvar. He is known for his works in Marathi literature, particularly 'Jñāneśvarī', a devotional commentary on Jñāneśvar's 'Jñāneśvarī'.
